subject: GPU pod rightsizing & latency SLOs for Acme private deployment
messages:
From: Luis Torres <luis.torres@acme.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Grant <emily.grant@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial capacity ask - private GPU pool for inference (on-prem)

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

We had a quick architecture sync internally and want to capture a concrete sizing ask so procurement can lock in the hardware window. High-level: Acme will run a private Redwood deployment inside our VPC-connected colo. Primary workload is real-time inference for our robot coordination agent (3k tokens per session average, but many short messages too). Target steady-state throughputs are ~450–600 tokens/sec aggregated with 75th pct latency target of <120ms per token for the critical path.

Questions for your sizing and networking guidance:
- Initial committed throughput target: 600 tokens/sec (burst to 900 for short windows)
- Expected concurrency: ~40 active chat sessions (p99 session concurrency distribution attached)
- Preferred hardware: 2–4 H100 DGX-style nodes (we can procure) — does that align?
- Network: our colo has 100Gb uplinks; we will peer to your control plane over a private VPN. Any special NIC recommendations?

Attaching: capacity_model_estimate.xlsx + network_diagram_v2.png. We're trying to finalize SOW by next week. Can we get a short written sizing recommendation and a note on autoscale / fallback policy you recommend for an on-prem private cluster?

Thanks,
Luis
Luis Torres
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Robotics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Luis Torres <luis.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 20:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask - private GPU pool for inference (on-prem)

Luis — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Quick summary of what we'll deliver in the recommendation pack:
- Rightsized GPU pod count for 600 tokens/sec steady-state with 900 tokens/sec burst buffer
- Latency SLO analysis (per-token and end-to-end) with suggested batching windows and quantization profile tradeoffs
- Network and NIC sizing (egress/ingress, RDMA vs TCP) and control-plane VPN best-practice
- Autoscale policy: cold-start/burst strategy and preferred canary rollout for model updates

Initial working assumptions (please confirm):
1) Model family: 7–13B transformer family (int8 quantized recommended for cost/throughput tradeoffs), KV cache reuse between messages assumed for session affinity.
2) Avg request size: 3k tokens/session, but median request often <300 tokens (chat turns).
3) SLO focus: 75th token latency <120ms; p95 <220ms if under autoscale.

Rishi, can you run a quick pod-rightsizing calc for 600 steady tokens/sec (assume H100 80GB, mixed precision int8 runtime)? Aim to return a 1-page table (pods, expected tokens/sec per pod, expected p75/p95 latencies, and recommended batching 10–30ms) by Monday.

Luis — we'll also include an ops runbook for graceful fallback: when local capacity >80% for 30s, route non-critical traffic to Redwood hosted fallback or a smaller quantized model. That can be a toggle in the SOW.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask - private GPU pool for inference (on-prem)

Jordan / Marissa — ran a micro-benchmark locally with 7B int8 and a 13B int8 on an H100 node (80GB). Notes:
- Baseline single H100 (no noisy neighbors): 180–220 tokens/sec sustained for 7B int8 with ~40ms p75 per-token.
- 13B int8: 85–110 tokens/sec sustained, ~70ms p75 per-token.
- Batching window tradeoffs: 10ms batching yields ~5–12% throughput improvement vs 0ms; 25–30ms batching gives up to ~20% but increases average per-token latency by ~15ms.

Preliminary rightsizing (assume mix of 70% 7B and 30% 13B workload):
- Effective tokens/sec per H100: ~170 tokens/sec.
- To reach 600 tokens/sec steady: 4 H100 nodes (3 active, 1 buffer for maintenance/failover).
- For 900 tokens/sec burst sustain for ~60s: recommend 6 H100 nodes total (autoscale headroom), or enable hosted fallback path for the excess.

Network notes:
- Recommend 100Gb links with RoCE enabled for RDMA if you're doing multi-node KV cache sharing; otherwise TCP with jumbo frames is acceptable.
- Control plane VPN: mutual TLS + 2FA for control-plane auth; lease renewal every 4h for session tokens.

I'll prepare a single-slide summary and a spreadsheet with latency/throughput per node for the SOW.

-Rishi
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Luis Torres <luis.torres@acme.ai>

This is exactly the level of detail we needed — thanks Rishi. A couple follow-ups:
- Can you include an explicit failure scenario (e.g., node OOM or NIC failure) and the expected mitigation timing in the ops runbook?
- For canary deploys: we'd like canaries limited to 5% traffic with automatic rollback after two failed health checks within 5 mins. Confirm Redwood tooling supports that out-of-the-box for private deployment.
- Procurement question: if we commit to 4 H100s with 2yr support, can we get a price credit for reserved capacity on the Redwood side (to cover the dedicated control-plane SLA)? Emily is copied to drive that thread.

Luis
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Thanks — tagging answers inline and next steps: 
- Failure scenarios: yes. We'll include three templates in the ops runbook (OOM/restart, NIC loss/partition, noisy neighbor). Expected mitigation timings: node restart <5 mins (auto-restart), failover routing <30s, full restore with replacement ~2–4 hours depending on procurement.
- Canary: Redwood private control plane supports traffic percentage canaries, auto-rollbacks on health-check failures, and staged model rollouts. We'll put the default canary to 5% with the two-failed-health-checks rollback rule in the SOW.
- Pricing/credits: Marissa, can you own a reserved-control-plane discount proposal for a 2yr hardware commit with quarterly billing? Emily, Jordan/Marissa will provide a written SOW + capacity appendix by Tue EOD that you can feed to procurement.

Next steps (action owners):
- Rishi: Deliver one-sheet + spreadsheet with per-node throughput numbers (due Tue 2026-12-08 10:00 UTC).
- Marissa: Pricing/discount proposal and SOW cover note (due Tue 2026-12-08 17:00 UTC).
- Jordan: Ops runbook draft and fallback policy text (due Wed 2026-12-09).

I'll attach the draft SOW (redwood_sow_draft_v1.pdf) to the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder.

Best,
Jordan
